newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-S.AFRICA RESTRICT INDIA TO 191-9 IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-S.AFRICA RESTRICT INDIA TO 191-9 IN FINAL.

text.p: Tight South African bowling and fielding - and the needless run out of Mohammad Azharuddin for 60 - restricted India to 191 for nine from 50 overs in the one-day triangular series final on Wednesday.
A confident Azharuddin was run out in the 46th over, just as India were looking to accelerate, after batting partner Nayan Mongia failed to respond to his call for a comfortable single to mid-on.
Earlier, the innings also lost momentum after a brilliant catch by Jonty Rhodes removed Sachin Tendulkar for 32 just when the Indian captain was beginning to dominate the attack.

Fast bowlers Allan Donald, with two for 23, and Lance Klusener, with two for 35, were the chief wicket-takers as disciplined out-cricket ensured India failed to reach an overall run-rate of four an over.
From the relative prosperity of 116 for two, they lost seven wickets while adding only 75 more runs.
After winning the toss and batting first in hot and humid conditions, India were initially strangled by accurate new ball bowling from Donald and Shaun Pollock.
But the left-handed Saurav Ganguly and Tendulkar increased the tempo as they added 43 in 11 overs before Ganguly (18) was run out via a direct hit from Pat Symcox at mid-off.
Tendulkar, after a sketchy start, began to threaten an innings of substance as he struck six fours in only 26 balls.

But the very next delivery, bowled by Klusener, led to his undoing. Cutting powerfully, Tendulkar saw a diving Rhodes at backward point pull off a superb catch and, once again, the Indian innings had to be reconstructed.
Rahul Dravid (33) and former Indian captain Azharuddin added 62 for the third wicket but, when Azharuddin was needlessly run out after his mix-up with Mongia, the rest of the innings crumbled.
